project_comments.note:
Two cross-cutting structural patterns were identified across WP-002 through WP-005 that should be addressed together in a follow-up refactor WP:

1. INLINE PIPELINE TYPE ARRAYS: Three separate locations hardcode pipeline type arrays as string literals — allPipelineTypes in getProjectManagerAction (PM P3 loop), the ['implementation', 'qa', 'code-review'] upstream types array in getDocumentationAction P1b, and the same pattern in the Reviewer P1b inline OR. If a new pipeline type is added in the future, all three sites must be updated manually or they will silently omit the new type. Recommend deriving from a single canonical PIPELINE_TYPES constant in constants.ts.

2. MISSING hasDependencyBlocked GUARD IN getDocumentationAction: getDeveloperAction, getQaAction, and getReviewerAction all call hasDependencyBlocked(wpDetail, rootIndex) at the top of their WP evaluation loop. getDocumentationAction omits this guard, relying on canStartWorkPackage at P7 instead. This is functionally correct (BLOCKED WPs are filtered at the loop header; IN_PROGRESS WPs are already dependency-validated) but creates an architectural inconsistency that could mislead future developers auditing the action functions. Recommend aligning getDocumentationAction with its peers.

Both items are non-blocking for current correctness but represent technical debt in the workflow-next-action.ts module.

Synthesis complete. Key cross-cutting findings: (1) Three inline PIPELINE_TYPES arrays across PM/Doc/Reviewer P1b — all flagged independently by Developer, QA, Reviewer — should be unified into a constants.ts constant to prevent drift. (2) getDocumentationAction omits the hasDependencyBlocked loop guard present in all peer action functions — architecturally inconsistent, functionally safe nowbut medium-priority cleanup. (3) GOLD NUGGET: state-machine timeline block in WP-006 integration test is exemplary test documentation — recommend adopting as project convention for all temporal test scenarios. (4) workflow-batch-actions.ts default: return [] branch now silently absorbs 9+ new action types — follow-up WP recommended to add explicit next_steps for each. Final test count: 774/774.
